title: The Leech Cure
text: A marsh doctor in a coat of eel skin offers to bleed your wounded with his prize leeches. He keeps them in a jar, fat and black and writhing. He swears by them. He has a great many grateful patients, he says, though none of them are here.

options.label: Let him bleed the wounded, and trust his prize leeches.

outcomes.text: Pale, and on the mend, with little round scars.
The leeches are not his prize ones, and they leave something behind.

options.label: The sharpest asks to see his notes, before anyone bares an arm.

outcomes.text: Gibberish, mostly, but one good recipe in it.

options.label: Refuse his leeches, politely. You have bled enough.

outcomes.text: He sulks into the reeds. His leeches do not: at dusk you find them on your legs, fat and sleepy.
